_sunset._note: Multispectrum-review is the canonical doctrine spec — it does NOT itself sunset on a calendar; individual facet-version increments (v2.0 → v2.1 → v2.3) are handled via supersedes_version. Schema present to satisfy ADR-0108 baseline; the in-spec prose references to `sunset_at_date` belong to the F13-migration facet (a CHECK on changesets), not to this spec's own lifecycle.

title: MultispectrumReview
description: Machine-readable mirror of docs/standards/multispectrum-review.md. Defines the seven-facet review bar, the closed change_class enum, the rigor matrix, the trigger-question registry, and the per-changeset evidence schema. Consumed by oya-check-dependency-seam (and successor lanes) for mechanical enforcement.

_meta.primary_consumer: agentic_flow (autonomous masterplan execution per ADR-0054 grit + ADR-0069 active-artifact-contract). Human dev_flow is secondary. Agents are the canonical reader of this spec.
_meta.machine_optimization_policy: Schema-strict (closed enums, typed required fields, indexed by id). Narrative belongs in docs/standards/multispectrum-review.md, NOT in this file. Long _description / rendering_examples / lane_implementation_note blocks are non-canonical pointers; FixupTask F-SPEC-PROSE-SLIM trims them. Files are read once per agent turn; minimize parser cost.
_meta.v2_directive: User directive 2026-05-14: 'additional spectrums that we should enforce into every single thing we do. including foundry. foundry's agentic flow + our current dev flow. should be enforced.' v2.0.0 adds F8 performance, F9 compliance as REQUIRED facets, and M1 challenge_assumption + M2 zoomed_out_fit as OPTIONAL meta-facets (required when meta_review_triggered).
_meta.v2_1_directive: User directive 2026-05-14: 'Make sure we add deterministic layer to it where it makes sense to do so.' v2.1.0 adds F10 reversibility/blast-radius, F11 observability, F13 migration/backwards-compat as REQUIRED facets when applicable + a `deterministic_layer_principle` declaring per-facet auto_checks vs human_judgment split. Lane enforces auto_checks mechanically; judgment layer fills the rest.
_meta.v2_3_directive: User directive 2026-05-15 across two consecutive messages: 'additional lens for our own policy adherence like naming, documentation, structure, architecture, dependency, etc' + 'schema, algorithm, as well'. v2.3.0 adds a new family of POLICY-ADHERENCE facets (A-prefix: A1..A7) distinct from F-family critique lenses and M-family meta lenses. A-facets mechanically enforce drift between code-as-built and doctrine-as-declared. Closed enum cap relaxed for A-family — adherence facets grow as policy domains do.
evidence_sources: foundry agentic-flow (oya vcs claim → work → verify → done → promote) with rtk-ai/grit compatibility/provenance only
_meta.session_start_directive: Every session — agentic OR human-dev — reads this spec before any code change. Quality bar is durable across sessions AND across agents.
_meta.purpose: Machine-readable mirror of docs/standards/multispectrum-review.md. Defines the seven-facet review bar, the closed change_class enum, the rigor matrix, the trigger-question registry, and the per-changeset evidence schema.

agentic_flow.description: Multi-agent autonomous masterplan execution per Oya VCS state machine; ADR-0054/grit-era rows are compatibility/provenance only during cutover.
trigger_points: oya vcs claim — agent declares intent and slice; multispectrum spec MUST be read
work iteration — every iterative-fix-loop cycle re-evaluates facets
verify — evidence file emitted to /evidence/multispectrum/ before oya vcs done
oya vcs done — emits evidence-backed ChangeBundle/completion payload after lane sub-check `multispectrum-evidence-attached` passes for the changeset
oya vcs promote — controller-owned promotion only after claim coverage, provider evidence, audit-chain coverage, and multispectrum evidence pass
review-fix loop — reviewer comments or CI failures become FixupTasks tagged to the violating facet
agentic_flow.mechanical_enforcement: Oya VCS admission plus oya-check-dependency-seam composite lane sub-checks (multispectrum-evidence-attached + fixture-pair-coverage + change-class-declared) refuse promotion when evidence is absent / non-canonical / incomplete.

dev_flow.description: Human-authored PR / code-review path AND mixed human-agent flows.
trigger_points: PR open — pre-PR checklist (/templates/checklists/pre-pr-multispectrum.json) filled by author or assigned agent
code review — reviewer maps comments to facet ids (F1..F9 / M1..M2)
merge gate — same lane as agentic_flow; no separate path
release tag — additional F8 performance + F9 compliance rigor; meta-facets M1/M2 re-evaluated against major-version changes
dev_flow.mechanical_enforcement: Same lane as agentic_flow plus CODEOWNERS check that reviewer signature is accompanied by facet-mapped comment (F-MULTI-CODEOWNERS-FACET-CITE).

enforcement_scopes.applies_to: every changeset across every layer: kernel, domain, application, app, adapter, infrastructure, cli, rest, grpc, graphql, worker, sdk, AND check-namespace lanes. No exemptions without an ADR-tracked carve-out.
enforcement_scopes.non_negotiable_floor: F1..F9 always required (rigor per change_class). M1/M2 required when meta_review_triggered (CC-1 kernel public API + CC-5 doc-only adding new ADR/standard/spec).

principles_reference._note: Doctrine principles P0..P9 are canonical at /specs/oyatie-doctrine.json#principles. This spec inherits and applies them; it does NOT redeclare. Per oyatie-doctrine.json#consolidation_policy.
principles_reference.applies_to_this_spec: Multispectrum review IS the lane-mechanical enforcement vehicle for these principles on every changeset.

deterministic_layer_principle._description: Per user directive 2026-05-14: every facet has TWO tiers — Tier 1 deterministic (mechanical checks the lane runs automatically) and Tier 2 judgment (human / agent findings + rationale). The lane REFUSES the changeset when Tier 1 auto_checks fail; Tier 2 judgment fills the rest. This prevents the multispectrum bar from being pure ceremony: every facet has a machine-enforceable floor.
tier_1_examples: F2 hyperscaler — `cargo deny check` exit 0 + no duplicate transitive versions
F3 adversarial — failing-fixture file present in expected path + `cargo test <fixture>` panics with expected diagnostic
F5 quality — `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0 + no `.unwrap()` or `.expect("...")` in non-test code per a configured allowlist
F7 security — `cargo audit` exit 0 + no RUSTSEC advisories + secret-scan over evidence files clean
F8 performance — benchmark file present at declared `benchmark_id` path + regression_baseline measurement attached
F9 compliance — `data_class_touched` array non-empty (even 'none' explicit) + audit_chain_emission flags coherent (required ↔ present)
F10 reversibility — feature_flag_id present OR migration_rollback_script_path present OR change_class ∈ {CC-4, CC-5, CC-7}
F11 observability — for each new public surface: structured-log-event-name registered in observability registry OR span_name declared
F13 migration — for breaking changes: ADR cite + version bump + sunset_at_date — all three present
consensus_debate — when required_when fires: synthesis file present at expected path with termination_reason ∈ allow-list
tier_2_examples: F1 Linus — judgment: are the data structures essential?
F2 hyperscaler — judgment: does this duplicate Cargo / cargo-audit / cargo-deny / cargo-public-api?
F6 alternatives — judgment: which alternative is selected and why?
F8 performance — judgment: what's the perf-budget regression-test that would catch a future degradation?
M1 challenge_assumption — judgment: is the premise still true?
M2 zoomed_out_fit — judgment: does this fit the system as architected?
deterministic_layer_principle.lane_implementation_note: Each facet's `evidence_required` block names the auto_checks the lane runs. When auto_check fails, lane refuses the changeset (severity = ramp-controlled per ADR-0092 D14). When judgment is missing/insufficient, lane reports-only — judgment is reviewer-enforced via CODEOWNERS + facet-mapped comment cite.

scorecard_schema._description: Derived view of evidence_schema rendered as a one-row-per-facet table. Per user directive 2026-05-14: 'Like a scorecard.' Replaces the wall-of-JSON view for at-a-glance review. Mechanically rendered by the seam lane from any evidence_schema instance + the rigor matrix for the declared change_class.

spec_version.description: multispectrum spec version this scorecard targets (e.g., 2.1.0)

rows.description: one row per applicable facet (F1..F13 plus M1/M2 when meta_review_triggered)

headline.description: one-line summary of the most important finding for this facet

summary_line.description: one-line human-readable summary, e.g., 'GREEN — 11/11 auto pass, 11/11 judgment ok, consensus n/a'

aggregate_rules.GREEN: every required facet: auto_checks ∈ {pass, n/a, not-yet-armed (report-only)} AND judgment ∈ {ok, n/a} AND consensus_debate_status ∈ {not-applicable, consensus-reached}
aggregate_rules.YELLOW: any required facet has judgment = needs-work OR consensus_debate_status ∈ {pending, in-progress}, AND no required facet has auto_checks = fail
aggregate_rules.RED: any required facet has auto_checks = fail OR consensus_debate_status = escalated OR mandatory artifact for the change_class is missing

rendering_examples.tabular_human_one_line_per_facet:
F1 Linus            | deep | ✓ pass | ✓ ok          | no special cases introduced
F2 Hyperscaler      | deep | ✓ pass | ✓ ok          | seam audit 6→1 crate
F3 Adversarial      | deep | ✓ pass | ✓ ok          | 78 F3 fixtures (passing+failing pairs)
...
rendering_examples.json_dashboard: consumed by per-repo PR-rollup dashboards; aggregate.overall feeds the merge-gate badge

scorecard_schema.lane_implementation: FixupTask F-LANE-SCORECARD-RENDER: extend oya-check-dependency-seam with `render_evidence_scorecard(evidence_path) -> Scorecard` reading an evidence_schema instance + the per-CC rigor matrix from this spec, emitting both JSON + tabular human form. Day-1 schema only; render fn lands in F-LANE-SCORECARD-RENDER.

consensus_debate_protocol._description: Multi-LLM (or multi-reviewer) debate-and-synthesize loop. Per user directive 2026-05-14: 'Round 1: All providers answer the question normally; Round 2: each provider sees others' responses and provides rebuttals; Synthesis: incorporates debate insights, consensus shifts, and unresolved tensions; iterate until consensus is reached.'

round_1_independent.purpose: Each reviewer answers independently, without seeing others' answers. Prevents anchoring bias.

round_2_rebuttals.purpose: Each reviewer sees other Round 1 answers + writes a rebuttal: which points they agree/disagree with, why.

synthesis.purpose: Synthesis owner (human reviewer OR designated LLM) consolidates consensus + disputes + unresolved tensions.

required_when: M1_challenge_assumption fired (premise of change being questioned)
M2_zoomed_out_fit fired (whether it belongs in the system)
CC-1 kernel public API change touching cross-microservice contract
new spec/standard/ADR that competes with existing primitives

tools.claude: in-session via Agent tool dispatching one subagent per facet (see executor_topology); never a single in-session reviewer across multiple facets
tools.codex: via oh-my-claudecode:ask skill with model=openai or via direct /ask codex; one invocation per facet
tools.gemini: via oh-my-claudecode:ask skill with model=gemini or via direct /ask gemini; one invocation per facet
tools.human: via PR review channel; evidence captured by author transcribing the comment trail into the debate format

executor_topology._directive_source: User directive 2026-05-14 (across two messages): 'consensus debate should be done by separate subagents or separate teammate sessions' + 'with each spectrum as their lens'.
executor_topology.rule: Each applicable facet (F1..F13 + M1/M2 as required) MUST be reviewed by its own separate subagent or separate teammate session, with that one spectrum/facet as the lens. A single reviewer_id MUST NOT appear across multiple facets within a single debate change_id — this would indicate bias-collapsed single-agent multi-facet execution and the lane MUST refuse.
executor_topology.rationale: A single agent reviewing all facets sequentially anchors its Round-2 rebuttals on its own Round-1 answers (bias collapse). Separate per-facet subagent execution produces true independence; synthesis sees real disagreement instead of self-rationalization.
dispatch_mechanisms: Claude Agent tool with subagent_type chosen per facet (e.g., code-reviewer for F5, security-reviewer for F7, oh-my-claudecode:critic for M1)
/oh-my-claudecode:team mode with N agents (N = number of applicable facets)
Cross-tool: claude facet + codex facet + gemini facet via /ask in distinct invocations
executor_topology.lane_validation_addition: F-LANE-DEBATE-SUBCHECK MUST validate (a) per-facet r1+r2 files present from distinct reviewer_ids, (b) NO reviewer_id appears across multiple facets, (c) synthesis termination_reason ∈ {consensus_reached, escalation_resolved}.

consensus_debate_protocol.lane_enforcement: When required_when triggers fire, oya-check-dependency-seam refuses the changeset unless /evidence/debate/<change_id>-synthesis.json exists AND its termination_reason ∈ {consensus_reached, escalation_resolved} AND per-facet r1/r2 files exist from distinct reviewer_ids (no single reviewer across multiple facets) per executor_topology rule.
consensus_debate_protocol.fixuptask_for_full_impl: F-LANE-DEBATE-SUBCHECK — extend the seam lane with a `consensus-debate-evidence` sub-check that scans /evidence/debate/ + verifies the synthesis file shape AND enforces the executor_topology rule (distinct reviewer_id per facet).

alias_map._description: User vocabulary 2026-05-14 directive maps to canonical facet ids. Reviewers may name any synonym; lane normalizes to the canonical id when validating evidence.

F1_linus.name: Linus critique
F1_linus.scope: code shape, data structures, special cases
trigger_questions: Are there special cases that could be deleted by reshaping the data?
Are the data structures essential, or did we accidentalize complexity?
Would deleting this entire piece of code lose anything?
Is there a smaller representation that holds the same invariants?

evidence_required.fixuptasks: array of bounded-fixuptask ids (may be empty)

F2_hyperscaler.name: Hyperscaler critique
trigger_questions: Does this scale to 10x-100x current load (deps, crates, requests, agents, tenants)?
Does this duplicate Cargo / cargo-audit / cargo-deny / cargo-public-api / existing tooling?
Should this be generated from a single source of truth instead of authored?
What's the failure mode at provider rate-limit / quota / cache-eviction?

evidence_required.fixuptasks: array of bounded-fixuptask ids (may be empty)

F3_adversarial.name: Adversarial critique
F3_adversarial.scope: tests designed to fail when invariants break, not just pass when invariants hold
trigger_questions: How would I break this?
Did a test actually walk the breaking path?
Is there a failing fixture proving the lane catches the violation?
Do all branches have at least one test, or only the happy path?

evidence_required.failing_fixture_added: bool — required true for new lane sub-checks AND new kernel public-API
evidence_required.passing_fixture_id: string — points to the canonical passing fixture
evidence_required.failing_fixture_id: string — points to the canonical failing fixture
evidence_required.diagnostic_asserted: string — the specific error/diagnostic the failing fixture asserts

F4_ergonomic.name: Ergonomic critique
F4_ergonomic.scope: new-contributor cognitive load, failure modes, copy-paste hazards
trigger_questions: How many minutes does a new contributor need to add/use this correctly?
What's the failure mode when someone makes a typo or partial fill?
Does the error message tell them exactly what to fix?
Does this require memorizing more than 3 things?

F5_quality.name: Quality critique
F5_quality.scope: code-shape issues in touched files independent of the stated goal
trigger_questions: Are there type misnomers (names that contradict the doc)?
Are there approximate algorithms where exact ones exist?
Are there hot locks where lock-free is feasible?
Are there panics/unwraps in library code where Result is feasible?
Are there silent drops of data where errors should propagate?

evidence_required.fixuptasks: array of bounded-fixuptask ids (may be empty)

F6_alternatives.name: Better-alternative critique
F6_alternatives.scope: what's the better way — named, rejected, or deferred with reason
trigger_questions: What's the better way to do this?
Why not that way?
If 'later', is there a bounded FixupTask with priority + reasoning?
Did I consider at least one Linus-style and one hyperscaler-style alternative?

evidence_required.rejected_reasons: array of strings (one per non-selected alternative)

F7_security.name: Security review
trigger_questions: Does this open or close attack surface?
DoS class: unbounded inputs, missing timeouts, hot-loop possibilities?
Data-integrity class: injection, traversal, header-smuggling, race conditions?
Correctness class: case-sensitivity, encoding edges, silent drops?
If this touches secrets: are they handled per the SecretReference contract?
If this touches tenant-scoped data: is data_class declared, RLS enforced, audit-chain emitted?

F8_performance.name: Performance / perf-budget review
F8_performance.scope: allocations, hot paths, latency budgets, throughput ceilings, copy semantics
trigger_questions: Does this allocate on a hot path? At 10× current load, what breaks?
Does a benchmark exist to prove the perf claim, or are we relying on intuition?
What's the perf-budget regression test that would catch a future degradation here?
Are zero-copy paths preserved, or did we introduce a copy that wasn't there before?
Does this change interact badly with cache locality, branch prediction, or async scheduling?

evidence_required.benchmark_id: string — path or symbol of the bench
evidence_required.regression_baseline: string — prior measurement reference if applicable

F9_compliance.name: Compliance / auditability / data-class review
F9_compliance.scope: regulatory class, auditability, data-class declaration, audit-chain emission, secret handling
trigger_questions: What data class does this touch? (Public, INTERNAL_ONLY, TENANT_SCOPED, PHI, PCI, …)
Does this need to emit to the audit-chain (ADR-0069)? If yes, is the emission wired?
Are secrets handled via SecretReference (no raw secrets in repo / chat / evidence)?
Does this touch RLS / tenant-scoping boundaries? Is the boundary still intact?
Does this change require a regulatory pack update (KR, EU, US, etc.)?
Are the changes auditable — can a compliance team answer 'who, when, what, why' from the evidence trail?

evidence_required.data_class_touched: array of strings — enum subset of {public|internal_only|tenant_scoped|tenant_payload|phi|pci|pipa|children|none}
evidence_required.secret_handling_path: string — enum of {secret-reference|n/a|adr-bypass} with ADR cite if bypass
evidence_required.regulatory_packs_impacted: array of strings — pack ids (e.g., oya-pack-kr)

M1_challenge_assumption.name: Challenge underlying assumption (meta)
M1_challenge_assumption.scope: premise of the change — is this the right problem to solve, or are we solving the wrong thing?
M1_challenge_assumption.required_when: meta_review_triggered — CC-1 kernel public API change OR new ADR/standard/spec OR breaking-API change OR new microservice
trigger_questions: What's the PREMISE this change is built on? Is the premise still true?
Could the entire need for this change be eliminated by changing something upstream?
Is there a hidden assumption (e.g., 'this is a problem at our scale') that may not hold?
Who decided this was the right problem to solve, and on what evidence?
If we did nothing here, what actually breaks — and is that breakage real?

evidence_required.premise_stated: string — what assumption underlies this change
evidence_required.premise_evidence_ref: string — pointer to data / measurement / ADR establishing the premise
evidence_required.do_nothing_consequence: string — what breaks if this change is deferred

F10_reversibility.name: Reversibility / blast-radius review
F10_reversibility.scope: rollback cost, feature-flag presence, blast radius of a wrong landing
F10_reversibility.required_when: CC-1 (kernel public API) OR CC-2 (adapter/infrastructure touching IO / state) OR any change crossing a microservice boundary OR any data-migration touching change
trigger_questions: If this lands and is wrong in production, what does rollback cost?
Is the change behind a feature flag, or is it ON for all tenants the moment it merges?
Are there forward-only steps (migrations, contract version bumps) that prevent rollback? Is the rollback path documented?
What's the blast radius — single cell, single tenant, single region, or workspace-wide?
deterministic_checks: feature_flag_id grep in code OR migration_rollback_script_path file exists OR change_class ∈ {CC-4 refactor pure, CC-5 doc only, CC-7 test} (rollback-trivial)
if database-migration touched: forward+backward migration files both exist

F11_observability.name: Observability review
F11_observability.scope: structured logs, metrics, traces — can production failures be diagnosed from the evidence alone?
F11_observability.required_when: CC-1 kernel public API OR CC-2 adapter/infrastructure adding I/O surface OR any new HTTP route OR any new state machine OR any new background worker
trigger_questions: If this breaks at 3am in production, can the on-call diagnose it from logs + metrics + traces alone — or do they need to attach a debugger?
Are the log events structured (named keys, not freeform strings)? Are the metric names + label sets low-cardinality?
Is every new error path emitted at the correct severity?
For long-running operations: is there a span instrumented around the operation boundary?
Do the labels avoid leaking PII / tenant-scoped data / sensitive captures (S6 class)?
deterministic_checks: every new public fn that returns Result has at least one log/span emission on the Err path (grep heuristic)
metric label cardinality bounded (no path captures in label values per S6 class)
span_name declared for each new I/O boundary fn

evidence_required.diagnosability_walkthrough: string — short narrative: 'a failure here looks like X in logs, Y in metrics, Z in traces'

F13_migration.name: Migration / backwards-compatibility review
F13_migration.scope: schema changes, public-API contract changes, data-format changes, dep version bumps
F13_migration.required_when: any breaking change to a public surface (per ADR-0037 API stability tiers) OR any schema/migration file added OR any dep major version bump
trigger_questions: Does this break existing callers / clients / consumer SDKs? If yes, is the major version bump in place AND a sunset date set?
For schemas: is there a forward migration AND a backward migration? Are existing rows handled?
For dep bumps: is the changelog reviewed? Are there deprecated APIs we use that now break?
Is there a cutover path: deploy old + new in parallel; flip traffic; retire old after N days?
Per the user's 'no-silent-regression' rule: is this in the LEAN-a10 lane?
deterministic_checks: if [package].version major bumped: ADR cite present in CHANGELOG + sunset_at_date present
migration file count: forward+backward both present in db/migrations/ (or equivalent)
for dep major bumps: dependency-rationales.json row's version_pin reflects the new major

evidence_required.sunset_at_date: string — ISO 8601 date for old surface retirement, OR null
evidence_required.forward_migration_path: string — path to migration script, OR null
evidence_required.backward_migration_path: string — path to rollback script, OR null

M2_zoomed_out_fit.name: Zoomed-out fit (meta)
M2_zoomed_out_fit.scope: does this change belong in the system as architected — or is it parallel infrastructure that should be unified?
M2_zoomed_out_fit.required_when: meta_review_triggered — CC-1 kernel public API change OR new ADR/standard/spec OR new microservice OR new lane/protocol
trigger_questions: Does this duplicate an existing artifact in the repo (spec, standard, lane, registry)? If yes, why not extend the existing one?
Is there an industry-standard primitive (AWS COE / Google Design Doc / Microsoft 1ES / Oracle EngExc) we should adopt instead?
Does this fit ADR-0069's active-artifact-contract capability model, or is it parallel?
Does this fit ADR-0056's 12-layer enum + BNF? Or are we inventing a new layer category?
If we zoom out 1 year: does this change still belong where we put it?

evidence_required.existing_primitives_surveyed: array of strings — repo artifacts considered for extension instead
evidence_required.industry_primitives_surveyed: array of strings — external frameworks considered (AWS COE, Google Design Doc, etc.)

adherence_facets._description: A-family — POLICY-ADHERENCE facets (v2.3.0). Distinct from F-family critique lenses (Linus, hyperscaler, adversarial, etc.) and M-family meta lenses (challenge_assumption, zoomed_out_fit). Each A-facet enforces drift between code-as-built and a SPECIFIC own-policy domain (doctrine principle / ADR / standard). Per consensus_debate_protocol.executor_topology + feedback_consensus_debate_spectrum_lens_subagents — each A-facet runs in its own subagent context with one policy lens, never combined with other A- or F-facets.
adherence_facets._directive_source: User directive 2026-05-15: 'additional lens for our own policy adherence like naming, documentation, structure, architecture, dependency, etc' + 'schema, algorithm, as well'
adherence_facets._required_when: Any change touching the domain of a given A-facet REQUIRES that facet's subagent review. Triggers are mechanical per the file-set predicates below.
adherence_facets._cap_relaxation: evolution_policy.facet_addition's 'max 12 closed enum cap' applies to F-family only. A-family cap is OPEN — grows as policy domains do; new A-facets land via 1-ADR action per the user's 'etc' room.

A1_naming_adherence.name: Naming adherence
A1_naming_adherence.scope: P10 + P14 BNF kebab-case + version-suffix + filename rules per .omc/specs/oyatie-doctrine.json#P14_file_naming_layout
A1_naming_adherence.triggers_when: any new file added to /specs/, /registry/, /evidence/, /templates/, docs/decisions/, crates/, tools/ OR any rename touching these paths
trigger_questions: Does the filename follow kebab-case (ASCII lowercase + digit + hyphen + dot)?
If the artifact is versioned, does the filename carry -vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH suffix?
Does the path match <kind>/<scope>/<concept>-v<semver>.<ext> BNF for cross-cutting durables?
Does $id (if present) match the filesystem path?
Does the crate name match ADR-0056 BNF v4.1: oya-<microservice>-(<bc-tokens>-)?<layer>?
A1_naming_adherence.executor_topology_subagent_type: oh-my-claudecode:code-reviewer (or a future oh-my-claudecode:naming-reviewer specialized agent)
A1_naming_adherence.fixuptask_for_full_impl: F-LANE-ADHERENCE-A1-NAMING (extend oya-check-dependency-seam check_naming_convention to enforce v2.3.0 trigger set)

A2_documentation_adherence.name: Documentation adherence
A2_documentation_adherence.scope: P9 no-sprawl + DOC-CATALOG + doc class shape + thin-gateway pattern; cites docs/DOC-CATALOG.md + docs/standards/doc-style.md
A2_documentation_adherence.triggers_when: any docs/*.md added/edited OR any standards/ADR/PRD created/updated OR any spec _meta.doc_class declaration changed
trigger_questions: Does the doc declare doc_class + length_cap + authority_tier in frontmatter?
Is the doc registered in DOC-CATALOG.md with class + owner + length cap + 'Does NOT cover' clause?
Does the markdown restate content from a JSON/ADR partner (P9 sprawl)? If yes, slim to thin-pointer-gateway.
Is the doc length within its declared length_cap?
Are cross-references resolvable (no broken links to retired files)?

A3_structure_adherence.name: Structure adherence
A3_structure_adherence.scope: P11 + P14 directory layout + repo topology + kind/scope/concept BNF placement per .omc/specs/oyatie-doctrine.json#repository_layout
A3_structure_adherence.triggers_when: any new file or directory added; any move/rename touching first-class durable homes
trigger_questions: Is the file placed in its canonical durable home (/specs/, /registry/, /evidence/, /templates/, docs/decisions/, docs/standards/)?
Does any new durable land in .omc/ (forbidden post-2026-05-14 migration)?
Does the placement match the artifact's <kind> per BNF (registry → /registry/, evidence → /evidence/, etc.)?
Is the <scope> token correct (cross-cutting vs registered-microservice-name)?

A4_architecture_adherence.name: Architecture adherence
A4_architecture_adherence.scope: ADR-0056 12-layer enum + clean architecture inward-flow + kernel ◀── domain ◀── app ◀── { api, worker, adapter } ◀── runtime; cites docs/standards/clean-architecture.md
A4_architecture_adherence.triggers_when: any new crate added; any cross-layer dependency edited in Cargo.toml; any port trait moved across layers
trigger_questions: Does the new crate's name match BNF v4.1 oya-<microservice>-(<bc-tokens>-)?<layer>?
Does the crate's <layer> token match its actual dependency direction (kernel has no deps on domain; adapter may depend inward but not outward)?
Are port traits declared in kernel and impls in adapter (no impl-in-kernel violations)?
Does any crate cross-import another product's kernel directly (must go through Workflow + Ontology adapter layer per feedback_workflow_objectgraph_adapter_layer)?
Does the dep graph respect the 12-layer enum order?

evidence_required.layer_compliance_per_crate: array of {crate, declared_layer, dep_layers_observed, compliant: bool}

A5_dependency_adherence.name: Dependency adherence
A5_dependency_adherence.scope: ADR-0092 seam policy + dependency-rationales.json + cargo-deny + LTS pinning; cites docs/standards/dependency-policy.md
A5_dependency_adherence.triggers_when: any change to Cargo.toml workspace.dependencies; any new direct dep; any version bump
trigger_questions: Does every new direct dep have a registry row in /registry/dependency-rationales.json with rationale + owner + layer_seam + replacement_strategy?
Does cargo-deny check pass (license posture: no AGPL/GPL/SSPL/BUSL/RSAL in product code)?
Is the dep pinned to its LTS major.minor per the LTS roster?
Is the dep's isolated_in_crate respected (no seam violations per ADR-0092)?
Does the dep duplicate functionality already in workspace (cargo / cargo-audit / cargo-deny / cargo-public-api)?

A6_schema_adherence.name: Schema adherence
A6_schema_adherence.scope: P1 machine-optimized + JSON Schema $schema/$id/_meta + closed enums + required fields per active-machine-readable-artifact-contract
A6_schema_adherence.triggers_when: any new JSON spec/registry added; any $defs or required[] change; any schema version bump
trigger_questions: Does the JSON declare $schema (Draft 2020-12) + $id matching its filesystem path + _meta with required ADR-0069 9-capability fields?
Are enum values closed (no open string slot where domain is bounded)?
Are required fields explicit at every object level?
Does the schema validate (jsonschema-validator pass)?
If schema breaking-change: is version bumped + sunset_at_date present + ADR cited?

A7_algorithm_adherence.name: Algorithm adherence
A7_algorithm_adherence.scope: P3 deterministic-where-it-matters + approximate-vs-exact + complexity classes + algorithm choice rationale
A7_algorithm_adherence.triggers_when: any new algorithm/heuristic in code; any complexity-class change; any approximate-where-exact-feasible substitution
trigger_questions: What's the algorithm's complexity class (O(N), O(N log N), O(N^2))? Is it documented?
Where exact is feasible, is the algorithm exact (vs approximate)? If approximate: is the precision-tradeoff documented?
On determinism-critical paths (correctness/security/audit/contract-stability per P3 matters_for list): is the output bit-reproducible?
Is there a benchmark proving the algorithm meets perf budget at 10x/100x load?
Did the author consider at least one Linus-style (simple/exact) and one hyperscaler-style (sharded/parallel) alternative?

evidence_required.algorithms_introduced_or_changed: array of {fn_name, complexity_class, deterministic: bool, benchmark_path?}

mandatory_artifacts: ADR cite for the public-API choice

CC-2_adapter_or_infrastructure.description: Adapter or infrastructure-layer crate (provider binding, framework glue)

mandatory_artifacts: before/after symbol-set parity check (cargo metadata or grep)

deep.description: Must produce at least one finding OR explicit null_finding_reason. Trigger questions answered in evidence.

scan.description: Must record considered=true. Findings may be empty.

skip.description: Reserved for explicit not-applicable. Requires not_applicable_reason.

fixture_pair_layout_convention.purpose: Every lane sub-check ships with a passing fixture + a failing fixture so F3 (adversarial) is structurally enforceable.

convention.meta_test: crates/<lane-crate>/tests/fixture_pair.rs — asserts for every sub-check that the failing fixture triggers the documented diagnostic AND the passing fixture does not.

multispectrum-evidence-attached.description: Lane reads the changeset's evidence bundle; refuses if multispectrum_review block absent, any facet missing considered, or rigor-matrix violated.

fixture-pair-coverage.description: For every sub-check declared by a lane crate, refuses if passing/ and failing/ fixture directories are not both present and a meta-test asserts the diagnostic.

change-class-declared.description: Every commit/changeset declares change_class_id matching change_classes enum. Lane refuses if absent or non-canonical.

session_start_hook_contract.description: Every session reads docs/standards/multispectrum-review.md + this JSON at start so the bar is durable across sessions, not session-scoped to a particular agent's memory.
session_start_hook_contract.implementation_path: agents/settings/claude.settings.json — hook 'multispectrum-bar-on-session-start' injects a one-line reminder citing this spec.
session_start_hook_contract.fallback: If SessionStart hook missing or stale, root-hub-pointers.json carries the multispectrum_review pointer so any agent discovers it on the authority-first read.

evolution_policy.facet_addition_f_family: 1-ADR action; max 12 F-family critique facets total (closed enum cap to prevent dilution).
evolution_policy.facet_addition_a_family: 1-ADR action; OPEN — A-family adherence facets grow as policy domains do (per v2.3.0 user directive). No closed cap; cap rule relaxed because each A-facet corresponds to a distinct doctrine principle / standard / ADR that already governs its domain.
evolution_policy.facet_removal: Forbidden without superseded_by ADR + 90-day deprecation window.
evolution_policy.rigor_matrix_amendment: 0-ADR action; tracked in decision_log header of this JSON.
